title: Public API and OAuth
summary: Opens the REST API used by the front end to scripts, integrations, BI tools and third-party applications. This package owns the built-in OAuth 2.1 authorization server (authorization code + PKCE, consent per tenant, revocation), personal API tokens with scopes and expiry, service accounts for tenant automations, the fine-grained scope model, bulk operations (synchronous up to 100 items, background beyond with tracking), rate limiting per token and per tenant with RateLimit-* headers, and the published OpenAPI documentation. Cross-cutting conventions (cursor pagination, ETag, idempotency, Problem Details) are delivered by each functional package; here they are audited for consistency.

stories.title: Create and revoke personal API tokens with scopes
stories.i_want: to create personal API tokens limited to one tenant, some scopes and an expiry date
stories.so_that: my scripts can call the API with only the access they need
acceptance: Given I am signed in to a tenant, When I create a token with a name, scopes and an expiry, Then the token value is shown once and only its hash is stored
Given a valid token, When a script calls the API with it as a Bearer token, Then the call succeeds within my permissions and the token's scopes
Given a token without `tickets:write`, When it is used to create a ticket, Then the call is rejected with 403 and an insufficient_scope Problem Details code
Given an expired or revoked token, When it is used, Then the call is rejected with 401
Given a token issued for tenant A, When it is used on tenant B, Then the call is rejected
Given my tokens list, When I view it, Then I see each token's tenant, scopes, expiry and last use

tech.title: Create api_token table with hashed secrets
tech.description: Add `api_token` (tenant_id, account or service account owner, name, token prefix, secret hash, scopes array, expires_at, last_used_at, revoked_at) with RLS and an index on the lookup prefix. Secrets are random, high-entropy and stored hashed only.
done_when: Migration applies; integration test verifies RLS
Integration test verifies no plaintext secret is stored

tech.title: Authenticate Bearer tokens in the shared request layer
tech.description: In `crates/api`, add token authentication to the shared request layer: resolve the token by prefix, verify the hash in constant time, check expiry, revocation and tenant, set the tenant context (SET LOCAL) and attach scopes. Update last_used_at asynchronously. Every route declares its required scope.
done_when: Unit tests cover hash verification, expiry and scope matching
Integration tests cover valid, expired, revoked, wrong-tenant and insufficient-scope tokens on real PostgreSQL
A test fails if a route is registered without a required scope

tech.title: Expose personal token management endpoints
tech.description: Add endpoints to create (value returned once), list and revoke my tokens. A token can only carry scopes the owner is entitled to; expiry is mandatory with a tenant-configurable maximum.
done_when: Integration tests cover create, list, revoke, maximum expiry and entitlement checks
Angular client regenerated

tech.title: Build the API tokens section of My account
tech.description: In My account, build the personal API tokens `mat-table` (name, tenant, scopes as chips, expiry, last use, revoke icon button with aria-label) and a create `MatDialog` with scope checkboxes, expiry date picker and a one-time display of the value with a copy button.
done_when: Component unit tests cover creation, one-time display and revocation confirmation
axe check passes

stories.title: Define fine-grained API scopes
stories.i_want: every API operation to require a documented scope
stories.so_that: tokens and third-party applications only get the access they were granted
acceptance: Given the scope catalog (tickets:read, tickets:write, workload:read, workload:write, time:write, admin and others), When I read the API documentation, Then each operation shows its required scope
Given a token with scopes and a user with roles, When an operation is called, Then access requires both the scope and the user's permission on the node
Given an external account, When it obtains any token, Then internal-only scopes are never granted
Given a cookie session from the web front end, When an operation is called, Then scopes do not restrict it and only permissions apply

tech.title: Model scopes and the scope check in the domain crate
tech.description: In `crates/domain`, define the scope catalog as an enum with stable string codes and implication rules (write implies read, admin implies tenant administration operations), and a function combining scopes with effective permissions.
done_when: Unit tests cover parsing, implication rules and the scope x permission combination

tech.title: Annotate all routes with scopes in the OpenAPI contract
tech.description: Declare the required scope on every route and publish it as an OAuth2 security requirement in the utoipa-generated contract. Add a contract test listing every operation and its scope.
done_when: Integration test asserts every operation in the generated OpenAPI has a security requirement
Integration tests cover scope enforcement on one route per resource family

stories.title: Authorize a third-party application with OAuth 2.1
stories.i_want: to authorize an application such as an MCP client for one tenant and chosen scopes
stories.so_that: it can act on my behalf without my password, and I can revoke it anytime
acceptance: Given a registered client, When it starts the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256), Then I sign in if needed and see a consent screen naming the client, the tenant to choose and the requested scopes
Given I approve, When the client exchanges the code with the correct code_verifier, Then it receives an access token and a rotating refresh token valid for the chosen tenant only
Given a wrong code_verifier, a reused code or a redirect URI not registered, When the client calls the token endpoint, Then the request is rejected
Given I refuse consent, When I click Refuse, Then the client receives access_denied
Given an authorized application, When I revoke it from My account, Then its tokens stop working immediately
Given the authorization server metadata endpoint, When a client fetches it, Then it describes endpoints, PKCE methods and scopes as RFC 8414 requires

tech.title: Create OAuth client, grant, code and token tables
tech.description: Add `oauth_client` (client id, name, redirect URIs, public/confidential, hashed secret), consent grants (account, tenant, client, scopes, granted_at, revoked_at), authorization codes (hashed, PKCE challenge, expiry, used) and refresh tokens (hashed, family id for rotation and reuse detection). Tenant-scoped tables use RLS.
done_when: Migration applies; integration tests verify RLS and single-use code constraint

tech.title: Implement authorization, token and revocation endpoints
tech.description: Using a maintained MIT/Apache OAuth library where it helps, implement `/oauth/authorize`, `/oauth/token` (authorization_code with mandatory PKCE S256, refresh_token with rotation and reuse detection), `/oauth/revoke`, RFC 8414 metadata and the protected resource metadata needed by MCP clients. Exact redirect URI matching; short-lived access tokens bound to one tenant.
done_when: Unit tests cover PKCE verification, code expiry and refresh rotation logic
Integration tests cover full flow, wrong verifier, code reuse, refresh token reuse revoking the family, wrong redirect URI and wrong tenant
Library licenses pass cargo-deny

tech.title: Support client registration for MCP clients
tech.description: Allow tenant admins to register clients, and support dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) for public clients as expected by the MCP authorization specification, behind a tenant setting. Registered clients are listed for admins.
done_when: Integration tests cover admin registration, dynamic registration enabled and disabled
Unit tests cover redirect URI validation

tech.title: Build the consent screen and authorized applications list
tech.description: Build the OAuth consent page (client, signed-in user, tenant radio cards, scopes with readable descriptions from Transloco keys, MCP notice, Refuse and Authorize buttons) and the Authorized applications section of My account with revoke buttons.
done_when: Component unit tests cover tenant selection, refuse and authorize
axe check passes

tech.title: Add Playwright test for the OAuth authorization code flow
tech.description: End-to-end test with a test client: start the flow, sign in, pick a tenant, approve, exchange the code, call the API, revoke from My account and verify the token is rejected.
done_when: Playwright test passes in CI through `just`

stories.title: Manage service accounts for tenant automations
stories.i_want: to create service accounts with roles and tokens
stories.so_that: automations do not depend on a person's account
acceptance: Given I am a tenant admin, When I create a service account with a name, Then it appears in the members list as a service account
Given a service account, When I grant it node roles and create a token for it, Then the automation can call the API within those roles and the token's scopes
Given a service account, When it acts, Then the history records it as the author with origin API
Given I disable a service account, When its tokens are used, Then they are rejected
Given a service account, When anyone tries to sign in to the web interface with it, Then sign-in is impossible

tech.title: Model service accounts as tenant-scoped principals
tech.description: Add a service account principal (tenant_id, name, description, disabled_at, created_by) usable in role grants and as token owner, with RLS. It has no password and no global account.
done_when: Migration applies; integration test verifies RLS and grant usage

tech.title: Expose service account management endpoints
tech.description: Add admin endpoints to create, disable, list service accounts and manage their tokens; integrate them in permission computation and audit log authorship.
done_when: Integration tests cover create, grant, token use, disable, audit authorship and non-admin denial
Unit tests cover principal resolution

tech.title: Add service accounts to the members administration screen
tech.description: In the members and roles administration, add a Service accounts tab with a `mat-table`, creation dialog, role assignment reuse and token management dialog.
done_when: Component unit tests cover create, disable and token creation
axe check passes

stories.title: Run bulk operations on tickets with progress tracking
stories.i_want: to edit, transition or move many tickets at once
stories.so_that: I can reorganize work quickly from the interface or a script
acceptance: Given 100 tickets or fewer, When I submit a bulk edit, transition or move, Then it runs synchronously and returns a per-ticket result
Given more than 100 tickets, When I submit the operation, Then it is queued as a background job and I get a job id to track progress
Given a running bulk job, When I poll it or watch the real-time stream, Then I see processed, succeeded and failed counts and per-ticket errors
Given tickets I may not edit or transitions not allowed by the workflow, When the bulk runs, Then those tickets fail individually with a reason and the others succeed
Given a bulk request replayed with the same Idempotency-Key, When it arrives, Then no second operation is started

tech.title: Create bulk operation tracking table
tech.description: Add `bulk_operation` (tenant_id, requester, kind, payload JSONB, total, processed, succeeded, failed, per-item errors JSONB, status, idempotency key) with RLS.
done_when: Migration applies; integration test verifies RLS and idempotency key uniqueness

tech.title: Expose bulk edit, transition and move endpoints
tech.description: Add `/api/v1/tickets/bulk` endpoints that validate the selection (explicit ids or a query), run up to 100 items synchronously in per-ticket transactions reusing ticket services, and enqueue a job beyond that. Each item records history with its origin.
done_when: Integration tests cover sync path, async threshold, partial failures, permission and workflow errors and idempotent replay
Unit tests cover selection validation and threshold logic

tech.title: Process large bulk operations in the worker
tech.description: In `crates/worker`, process bulk jobs in batches with SKIP LOCKED, update progress counters, publish progress events on the outbox for real-time display, and resume safely after a crash.
done_when: Integration tests cover batch processing, two workers without double processing and resume after interruption

tech.title: Build bulk action bar and progress display
tech.description: In search results, add row selection and a bulk action bar (edit fields, transition, move) with dialogs, then a progress `mat-progress-bar` and a results summary listing failed tickets.
done_when: Component unit tests cover selection, dialogs, sync results and async progress
axe check passes

stories.title: Enforce rate limits per token, user, IP and tenant
stories.i_want: API calls to be rate limited per token, user, IP and tenant with standard headers
stories.so_that: one script or tenant cannot degrade the service for others
acceptance: Given a token under its limit, When it calls the API, Then responses include RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset headers
Given a token exceeding its limit, When it calls the API, Then it receives 429 with a Problem Details body and Retry-After
Given a tenant exceeding its API quota, When any of its tokens call the API, Then they are limited while other tenants are unaffected
Given several API instances, When the same token calls them, Then the limit is shared across instances
Given a tenant admin, When I view the tenant settings, Then I see the configured API quotas

tech.title: Implement distributed rate limiting middleware on Valkey
tech.description: Add an Axum middleware implementing a sliding-window or token-bucket limiter in Valkey (atomic script) keyed by token, user, IP and tenant, with limits from tenant settings and defaults from environment configuration. Emit RateLimit-* and Retry-After headers.
done_when: Unit tests cover limit resolution and header computation
Integration tests (real Valkey, two API instances) cover shared limits, tenant isolation and 429 responses

tech.title: Expose tenant API quota settings
tech.description: Add API quota fields to tenant settings (read for tenant admin, write for super admin) and show them in the tenant administration screen.
done_when: Integration tests cover read and write permissions
Frontend component unit test covers display; axe check passes

stories.title: Publish the OpenAPI contract and interactive documentation
stories.i_want: a published OpenAPI specification and interactive documentation served by the API
stories.so_that: I can build integrations and BI extractions without reading the code
acceptance: Given a running API, When I open the documentation URL, Then I see the interactive documentation generated from the current contract, self-hosted without third-party CDN
Given the contract, When I download it, Then it is a valid OpenAPI document describing every MVP resource family with scopes, errors and examples
Given a BI extraction, When I follow the documentation, Then I can page through tickets with cursors and select returned fields
Given a pull request changing the API, When CI runs, Then a breaking change against the previous v1 contract fails the build unless marked as an announced deprecation

tech.title: Serve the OpenAPI document and self-hosted docs UI
tech.description: Serve `/api/v1/openapi.json` and an interactive documentation page bundled locally (MIT/Apache UI, no CDN, GDPR). Enrich utoipa annotations with descriptions, examples and Problem Details error codes per operation.
done_when: Integration test fetches the document and validates it against the OpenAPI schema
Docs UI loads without any external request (test asserts CSP compliance)

tech.title: Add contract breaking-change check to CI
tech.description: Add a `just` recipe that compares the generated contract with the last released v1 contract using an MIT/Apache diff tool and fails on removals or incompatible changes; GitHub Actions calls it.
done_when: Recipe fails on a test fixture with a removed field and passes on an additive change
Recipe wired into CI

tech.title: Audit API conventions across all resource families
tech.description: Write contract-level integration tests checking, for every list endpoint, cursor pagination and field selection; for every update, ETag/If-Match; for every creation, Idempotency-Key; and for every error, RFC 9457 format with a stable code. Fix deviations in the owning packages.
done_when: Convention test suite runs in CI and passes for all MVP endpoints

tech.title: Write the public API guide
tech.description: Write `docs/en/api-guide.md` and its French version: authentication options, scopes, pagination, idempotency, ETag, errors, rate limits, bulk operations and a BI extraction example.
done_when: Guide reviewed; every code sample is executed by an integration test or a script in CI
